gaps.fact: Conversion formulas between metric and standard measures: hectolitres per hectare against tons per acre, and acres against hectares (about 2.47 acres to the hectare). Nothing in either bank or chapter converts a yield.

Phenolic ripeness versus sugar ripeness, and how vineyard choices (canopy, yield, hang time, site) move one against the other. Neither bank asks it and no chapter fact teaches it; the Codex gives Brix and potential alcohol, and only the ahr and naoussa articles name phenolic ripeness in passing.
Hangtime as a named stage of ripening after véraison, and vineyard aspect as the Court defines it (heat and light at different times of day).
Vitis vinifera is native to the Mediterranean, Europe and southwestern Asia and runs to about 10,000 varieties.
Collection bin size (large or small) and its effect on fruit quality on the way to the winery.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 119 (Viticulture & Winemaking 69, Soil & Terroir 50), Village 85 (Viticulture & Winemaking 29, Terroir: Climate & Soil 56), 204 in all. The shared category Viticulture & Winemaking is split by subject: of its 69 Régionale stems 38 are vineyard and 31 cellar; of its 29 Village stems 15 are vineyard and 14 cellar. The Certified column is well served: climate scales, degree days, moderators, rain shadows, the named soils, the vine cycle and training systems each have Village stems. Pierce's disease, a Certified fact, is keyed by one Régionale stem (i-rbxt0eth, Viticulture & Winemaking) and stands as a distractor in two more (Australia, United States); no Village stem or chapter fact carries it. Vintage charts are deferred by the Court to the regional pages and the Codex holds none by design. Two Court cells to read with care when writing our own copy: the Court writes 'Grafting of Vitis Vinifera onto Vitis Labrusca rootstock' where the rootstocks in use are riparia, rupestris and berlandieri crosses (the Codex says American species); and the Court calls phylloxera a vine louse while the Régionale stem i-x51uu5jl 'Phylloxera is what kind of organism?' keys 'A root-feeding aphid', an accepted simplification (the insect is an aphid relative) and not logged as an error. No law or classification change since 8.2023 touches these pages; no search was spent.
